overview: Pool Corporation is the world's largest wholesale distributor of swimming pool supplies, equipment and related leisure products, operating roughly 440-450+ sales centers across the US, Canada, Europe, and Australia under the SCP, Superior Pool Products, Horizon, National Pool Trends (formerly National Pool Tile), and Sun Wholesale Supply banners. The company also distributes irrigation and landscape maintenance products through Horizon, serving a highly fragmented base of pool builders, remodelers, retailers, service/repair companies, and irrigation/landscape contractors. Headquartered in Covington, Louisiana, POOL holds an estimated 35-40% share of the roughly $10B US wholesale pool products market, making it by far the largest player in an industry of mostly single-location independents.

business_model.summary: Pool Corp is a pure wholesale distribution intermediary: it buys pool chemicals, equipment, building materials, and leisure/outdoor-living products from manufacturers (Pentair, Zodiac/Fluidra, Hayward, and others) and resells them through its branch network to pool builders, remodelers, retailers, and service companies, earning a distribution margin rather than manufacturing products itself. Revenue is a mix of non-discretionary, highly recurring maintenance/chemical sales (relatively resilient, weather-and-pool-count driven) and more cyclical, discretionary new-construction and remodel/building-materials sales (sensitive to interest rates, housing, and consumer discretionary spending). Private-label and proprietary products (including POOL360 digital platform/private label lines) are a growing, higher-margin mix shift, with POOL360-related sales reaching roughly 18% of sales as of Q2 2026. Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional/repeat-purchase (not subscription) but underpinned by a large, aging installed base of 14+ million US pools that require ongoing chemicals, parts, and periodic remodeling regardless of new construction trends.

revenue_streams.name: Maintenance products (chemicals, supplies, replacement parts)
revenue_streams.trend: stable/resilient - non-discretionary, tied to installed base

revenue_streams.name: Building materials / remodel (incl. National Pool Trends tile, decking, pool surfaces)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - +4% in Q2 2026, share gains offsetting soft discretionary demand

business_model.customer_type: B2B wholesale - serves ~120,000+ mostly small/independent pool builders, remodelers, specialty retailers, service/repair companies, and irrigation/landscape contractors; highly fragmented customer base with no material customer concentration
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily United States with operations in Canada, Europe (France, UK), and Australia; international remains a small but growing share of the ~440-450 sales center network

main_competitors: Heritage Pool Supply Group (subsidiary of SRS Distribution, acquired by The Home Depot, 2024)
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant #1 wholesale distributor with an estimated 35-40% share of the ~$10B US wholesale pool products market (~$62B market including retail/service); the next-largest competitor, Heritage Pool Supply Group, holds roughly 8-10% share and is now backed by Home Depot's balance sheet following the ~$18.25B SRS Distribution acquisition, the most significant competitive structural change in years.

moat_factors.description: ~440-450+ sales centers provide same-day/next-day local availability that smaller distributors cannot match, critical for time-sensitive repair/maintenance parts and builder project timelines.

Scale purchasing from top suppliers (Pentair ~20%, Zodiac ~12%, Hayward ~11% of 2024 cost of products sold) gives pricing and allocation advantages difficult for smaller distributors to replicate, while diversification across these three plus others limits single-supplier dependency risk.

Customer base is overwhelmingly small/independent pool builders and service companies with limited switching incentive given local branch convenience, credit terms, and established relationships; no customer concentration risk.
Growing proprietary and private-label offerings (POOL360-related sales ~18% of sales in Q2 2026) improve margins and differentiate vs. pure pass-through distribution.

Decades-long track record of acquiring small independent distributors in a highly fragmented industry, extending density and product breadth (National Pool Trends/tile network, Horizon irrigation) ahead of less-capitalized competitors.

weaknesses: Home Depot's acquisition of SRS Distribution (parent of Heritage Pool Supply Group) materially increases the competitive capitalization of the #2 player, which has already completed ~20 independent distributor acquisitions in recent years and is reported to be gaining incremental wallet share, even if analysts view the current impact as modest

Highly exposed to discretionary new pool construction and remodel spending, which has fallen sharply since the 2020-2022 COVID-era surge as higher interest rates and reduced consumer discretionary spending have weighed on big-ticket purchases
Pronounced seasonality (Q2/Q3 are peak quarters) and weather dependency create quarterly earnings volatility
Gross margin pressure from elevated inbound freight costs and customer/product mix shift evident in 2026 (gross margin down ~30bps YoY through H1 2026)
Leadership transition risk: new CEO (John Watwood) appointed May 2026 after predecessor Peter Arvan's departure, with associated one-time transition costs embedded in FY2026 guidance

growth_drivers: Continued consolidation of the highly fragmented independent pool/irrigation distribution market through disciplined, bolt-on M&A — explicitly named one of new CEO Watwood's four stated priorities
Private-label and proprietary product penetration (POOL360 platform-related sales ~18% of sales and rising) driving mix-shift margin improvement
Horizon irrigation and landscape maintenance segment expansion, diversifying away from pure pool-industry cyclicality
National Pool Trends (formerly National Pool Tile) building materials network gaining share in remodel/renovation spending, up 4% in Q2 2026 even as broader discretionary demand stayed soft

Large, aging installed base of 14+ million US pools (many 20+ years old) creating structural, multi-year demand for resurfacing, equipment replacement, and automation/efficiency upgrades independent of new construction cycles
International expansion in Canada, Europe, and Australia, though still a modest share of the overall footprint

Eventual normalization/recovery of new pool construction and discretionary remodel demand as interest rates ease from post-2022 highs, representing potential cyclical upside not currently embedded in a muted 2025-2026 run-rate

business.description: New pool construction and discretionary remodel spending surged in 2020-2022 (pandemic-driven outdoor living boom) then declined sharply through 2023-2025 as higher interest rates and reduced consumer discretionary spending curtailed big-ticket, financed purchases; new construction remains down an estimated ~50% from the pandemic peak and the 2026 environment is still described by management as a 'muted discretionary market.'

business.risk: Intensifying competition from Home Depot-backed Heritage Pool Supply Group
business.description: Heritage (via parent SRS Distribution, now owned by Home Depot after an ~$18.25B deal) has completed roughly 20 bolt-on acquisitions of independent pool distributors in recent years and now has access to Home Depot's capital base, the most significant structural threat to POOL's historical #1 position; early read suggests modest, not dramatic, share erosion so far.

Many pool builder and remodeler customers are small, thinly capitalized businesses vulnerable to a prolonged construction downturn, credit tightening, or consumer pullback, which could pressure receivables and order volumes.

financial.description: Gross margin declined ~30bps YoY through H1 2026 (29.4% vs. 29.7% prior year) due to elevated inbound freight costs and unfavorable customer/product mix; full-year 2026 guidance assumes margin runs ~30bps below the prior year.

Total debt increased $110.8 million year-over-year to roughly $1.3 billion as of mid-2026, funding share repurchases and working capital amid soft organic growth; debt/equity around 1.35x and net debt/EBITDA around 2.6x leave moderate but not excessive leverage.

financial.risk: EPS growth muted relative to historical cyclical highs
financial.description: FY2026 guidance of $10.87-$11.17 adjusted diluted EPS (excluding CEO transition costs) remains well below the FY2022 cyclical peak (EPS of $18.89), reflecting the magnitude of the post-COVID demand reset even three-plus years on.

regulatory.description: Pool chemicals (notably chlorine-based products) are subject to EPA, DOT hazardous-materials transport, and state-level environmental regulations governing storage, handling, and distribution, adding compliance costs.

As a distributor of manufactured goods (many with imported components or finished products), POOL is exposed to tariff changes affecting input costs passed through the supply chain, an ongoing risk given elevated US tariff activity in 2025-2026.

macro.description: New pool construction and major remodels are frequently financed (home equity lines, consumer loans); elevated interest rates since 2022-2023 directly suppressed big-ticket discretionary purchases and remain the primary swing factor for a construction-demand recovery.

macro.risk: Housing market and consumer discretionary spending sensitivity
macro.description: New pool construction correlates with housing turnover, home equity levels, and discretionary consumer spending; a weaker housing market or consumer pullback would further delay the construction recovery, though the maintenance business (the majority of revenue) is comparatively insulated.

Peak sales and operating income occur in Q2/Q3; unseasonably cool or wet weather in peak months can meaningfully reduce chemical/maintenance sales and shift the pool season's timing, creating quarter-to-quarter earnings volatility.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The US pool industry is roughly a $62B market (wholesale distribution ~$10B) with 14+ million existing pools; maintenance spending represents an estimated ~64% of total market activity and is structurally resilient, while new pool construction remains roughly 50% below its pandemic-era peak. Industry commentary is cautiously optimistic that remodeling/renovation demand is beginning to pick up even as new construction stays soft, supported by the large base of pools now 20+ years old requiring resurfacing, equipment replacement, and automation upgrades.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high for the discretionary (new construction, major remodel) portion of revenue, which is sensitive to interest rates, housing, and consumer confidence; low cyclicality for the maintenance/chemical portion, which is tied to the installed base of existing pools and recurs regardless of macro conditions. The blended business is less cyclical than a pure homebuilder or pool manufacturer but still showed a pronounced boom (2020-2022) and bust (2023-2025) pattern.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High for new construction and discretionary remodel demand (financed purchases); low direct sensitivity for maintenance revenue. POOL's own balance sheet carries moderate debt (~$1.3B, D/E ~1.35x) with interest coverage around 11.6x, so rate sensitivity is primarily a demand-side risk rather than a balance-sheet refinancing risk.
key_input_costs: Steel, aluminum, and plastics used in pool equipment and building materials
Inbound freight/logistics costs (flagged as a 2026 margin headwind)

recent_developments.event: Q2 2026 results: net sales +2% to ~$1.8 billion (slightly below consensus of ~$1.82B); gross margin declined 30bps YoY to 29.7% on elevated inbound freight and mix; diluted EPS flat at $5.17, adjusted diluted EPS +4% to $5.38, beating the $5.34 estimate. Building materials grew 4% on National Pool Trends showroom/product breadth strength; POOL360 proprietary/private-label sales reached ~18% of sales. Management described 'steady maintenance demand' alongside a 'muted discretionary market.'

Full-year 2026 guidance confirmed/narrowed: GAAP diluted EPS of $10.66-$10.96 (includes ~$0.21 of CEO transition costs and $0.02 of ASU 2016-09 tax benefit); adjusted diluted EPS (excluding transition costs) of $10.87-$11.17, consistent with prior guidance. Full-year revenue guided to low-single-digit growth, driven mostly by pricing (~2-3%), with gross margin expected to run ~30bps below the prior year.

Board increased the share repurchase authorization to $600.0 million (adding $329.0 million to the $271.0 million remaining as of late April 2026) and raised the quarterly dividend 4% to $1.30/share — the company's 15th-16th consecutive year of dividend increases. Share repurchases over the trailing 12 months totaled $266.7 million.

CEO transition: John B. Watwood (joined as EVP in January 2026, prior operational leadership at Motion Industries/Genuine Parts) was appointed President and CEO effective May 4, 2026, succeeding Peter D. Arvan, who departed the role and the board. Board Chair John E. Stokely was named Executive Chair. New CEO stated four priorities: sales excellence, pricing and supply chain discipline, operational execution, and disciplined M&A.
H1 2026 results: net sales +4% to ~$3.0 billion; gross margin 29.4% (down 30bps YoY); diluted EPS +1% to $6.61, adjusted diluted EPS +5% to $6.80. Total debt rose $110.8 million YoY to ~$1.3 billion.

Home Depot's ~$18.25 billion acquisition of SRS Distribution (completed in 2024, continuing to integrate through 2025-2026) brought Heritage Pool Supply Group — POOL's largest wholesale competitor at an estimated 8-10% share — under Home Depot ownership, intensifying the competitive and capital landscape in pool wholesale distribution; Heritage has completed roughly 20 independent-distributor acquisitions in recent years, though analysts view share erosion to date as modest.

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO John Watwood (appointed May 2026) framed strategy around four priorities: sales excellence, pricing and supply chain discipline, operational execution, and disciplined M&A. On demand: 'steady maintenance demand from our installed base' and 'continued momentum in building materials' are offsetting 'a muted discretionary market' for new construction and major remodels. Management did not provide a specific timeline for new-construction recovery, continuing to frame FY2026 as a trough/stabilization year with pricing-driven rather than volume-driven revenue growth.

bull_case: Dominant, hard-to-replicate scale moat (35-40% share of US wholesale pool distribution, ~440-450 sales centers) generates durable distribution economics even in a soft demand environment, evidenced by continued margin resilience and a 15th-16th consecutive year of dividend increases through the downturn

Non-discretionary maintenance revenue (an estimated ~60% of sales, tied to a 14+ million installed base of aging pools) provides a resilient earnings floor largely independent of the new-construction cycle, limiting downside versus a pure homebuilder or pool-equipment-manufacturer exposure

New pool construction and discretionary remodel spending are running roughly 50% below the 2022 pandemic peak — a cyclical trough rather than a structural impairment — such that any eventual decline in interest rates or recovery in consumer discretionary spending represents meaningful earnings upside not currently priced into a run-rate well below FY2022's peak EPS of $18.89

Disciplined, decades-long M&A consolidation track record in a highly fragmented industry (~125,000 pool service businesses, most independents) continues under new CEO Watwood's explicitly stated 'disciplined M&A' priority, extending density and product breadth ahead of smaller competitors

Active capital return program ($600M buyback authorization, consistently rising dividend, ~$266.7M repurchased over the trailing year) supports EPS growth and signals management/board confidence even amid a multi-year demand trough
bear_case: Home Depot's acquisition of SRS Distribution placed Heritage Pool Supply Group — POOL's largest wholesale competitor — under the balance sheet of the largest home-improvement retailer in the US, materially raising the capitalization and acquisition capacity of the #2 player in a market POOL has long dominated unchallenged

New pool construction and discretionary remodel spending have not shown a clear inflection after three-plus years of decline (2023-2025 into a still-'muted' 2026), and FY2026 guided EPS of ~$10.87-$11.17 remains roughly 40% below the FY2022 cyclical peak, implying the earnings recovery thesis is entirely dependent on an uncertain-timing interest rate/housing cycle turn

Gross margin is under incremental pressure (down ~30bps YoY through H1 2026) from freight costs and mix shift, with full-year guidance assuming continued compression rather than recovery, indicating limited near-term operating leverage even if volumes stabilize

Leadership transition risk: a new, first-time CEO (Watwood, promoted after only months as EVP) took over in May 2026 following his predecessor's departure, introducing execution uncertainty during an already challenged demand environment, with one-time transition costs embedded in guidance

Rising absolute debt levels (~$1.3B, up $110.8M YoY) funding buybacks during a period of soft organic growth increases financial risk if the discretionary demand recovery is delayed further or interest rates stay elevated longer than expected
